_meta.what_this_is: Two samples of 100 request latencies (ms) for one endpoint: a baseline and a later regression. In both, 95 of 100 requests are fast (50ms). The regression pushes the slowest 5% from 200ms to 900ms -- a tail regression that hits 1 in 20 users on every request. The mean barely moves because 95% of requests did not change; the p99 moves a lot, because it lives in the tail that did.
_meta.data_is: A FIXTURE. The latency samples are hand-authored so the mean stays under a mean-based alert threshold while the p99 blows past the SLO -- the case where averaging hides a tail regression. Every statistic is computed in latency.py with the nearest-rank percentile.
_meta.format: samples: {name:[latency_ms,...]}; slo_p99_ms: the p99 the SLO allows; mean_alert_ms: the mean a naive monitor alerts on.
